name: Kingdom of Mysore
alt: Sultanate of Mysore (Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, 1761-1799)
Kingdom of Mysore under the Wodeyars

predecessors.name: Vijayanagara Empire
predecessors.text: the prefecture of Mysore, given to Yaduraya in 1399 under Harihara II

successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: Mysore as the Wadiyars held it after 1799, without Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada

ledger.x: 1399: Yaduraya is made prefect of Mysore under Harihara II of Vijayanagara.

1399: Yaduraya 'was made the prefect of Mysore and the surrounding regions by his overlord Harihara II', and his successors ruled 'under the vassalage of the Vijayanagara Empire' (Wadiyar page, reopened 2026-10-25; the same page gives 'until around 1553').
1572: Mysore stands independent on its core.
1610: Raja Wodeyar I takes Srirangapatna and moves the capital there.
1610: the capital moves from Mysore to Srirangapatna.
1613: the Wodeyars stop paying tribute to Vijayanagara's seat.
1673: Chikka Devaraja takes the throne (28 February 1673) and Cliopatria draws his whole reign's conquests from this year.
ledger.cp: Various (Maddagiri, Salem and Baramahal, Hassan, Chikmagalur, Tumkur: holders not named on the pages)

ledger.x: 1673: Coimbatore passes to Mysore in Chikka Devaraja's reign; the year is Cliopatria's bridge (his throne on 28 February 1673, Chikka Devaraja page).
1687: Chikka Devaraja gets Bangalore.
1694: the kingdom is 'extended by the addition of regions to the west up to the Baba Budan Mountains'.
ledger.cp: Western regions up to the Baba Budan Mountains (holder not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1700: Chikka Devaraja sends an embassy to Aurangzeb and receives 'a formal subordination to Mughal authority and a requirement to pay annual tribute' (Chikka Devaraja page, reopened 2026-10-25).
1724: bridge.
1761: Hyder Ali becomes ruler of Mysore.
1763: Hyder takes Keladi.
1766: Hyder annexes the Zamorin's Kozhikode.
29 March 1769: the Treaty of Madras ends the First Anglo-Mysore War, restoring the prior status quo except for Mysore's acquisition of Karur.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: November 1770: 'The Marathas responded in November 1770 with an invasion by an army of 35,000 men', 'captured much of north-eastern Mysore', failed to take Seringapatam in a siege of five weeks and 'instead took Bangalore' (Hyder Ali page, reopened 2026-10-25).
1772: 'Hyder finally sued for peace.
1772: the peace ends the fighting of the invasion that began in November 1770 ('In 1772 Hyder finally sued for peace', Hyder Ali page).

1773: 'In 1773, Hyder used this opportunity to send Tipu with an army to recover territories lost to the Marathas to the north' (Hyder Ali page, reopened 2026-10-25; the opportunity is the Maratha succession crisis after Madhavrao I).
1777: Hyder recovered Coorg and parts of the Malabar District from the Marathas (Kingdom of Mysore page).
1778: bridge inside 1776-1779.
ledger.cp: Dharwad and Bellary (holders not named on the pages)

ledger.x: 1779: Mysore is 'about 80,000mi2 (205,000km2)' under Hyder Ali, holding parts of modern Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
ledger.cp: Various (Dindigul, Baramahal, Cuddapah, Kurnool and Anantapur country: holders and years not on the pages opened)

ledger.x: December 1782: Hyder Ali dies (6 or 7 December, Hyder Ali page) and his son Tipu Sultan succeeds (Kingdom of Mysore page infobox: Tipu Sultan, 1782-1799).

18 March 1792: the Treaty of Seringapatam gives the Marathas the territory up to the Tungabhadra River ('The Peshwa acquired territory up to the Tungabhadra River'); the page names neither Dharwad nor Bellary.

18 March 1792: the Nizam receives the land from the Krishna River to the Penner River, plus the forts of Cuddapah and Gandikota on the Penner's south bank (the hyderabad-state dossier records the same gain and names Bellary among the Ceded Districts of this land).
18 March 1792: the British receive a large part of Mysore's Malabar Coast territory between Travancore and the Kali River, plus the Baramahal and Dindigul districts.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 18 March 1792: the rajah of Coorg was granted independence, though Coorg effectively became a Company dependency.
1799: after Seringapatam falls on 4 May 1799, Mysore 'ceded Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada to the British'.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 4 May 1799: Tipu falls at Seringapatam and the British restore Mysore to the Wadiyars.
1799: the capital returns from Srirangapatna to Mysore.
1831: the British take direct control of Mysore.
1834: Mark Cubbon, Commissioner from 1834, makes Bangalore the capital.
1881: power returns to the Wadiyars.
9 August 1947: Mysore joins the Indian Union.

wars.name: Bijapur's repulse of Mysore (siege of Srirangapatna, 1638)
wars.outcome: Chamaraja VI and Kanthirava Narasaraja I tried to expand north; Bijapur repelled them and the 1638 siege of Srirangapatna failed.

wars.name: Chikka Devaraja's Trichinopoly campaign
wars.outcome: In 1696 Chikka Devaraja attacked the Nayaks of Madura and besieged Trichinopoly; 'the siege of Trichnopoly had to be abandoned because the alliance had begun to rupture' (no date on the page).

wars.name: First Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Began in August 1767 with the attack on the Company outpost at Changama; Hyder reached within five miles of Madras and sued for peace.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of Mysore (Madhavrao's third war against Hyder)
wars.outcome: The Marathas invaded in November 1770 with 35,000 men, took much of north-eastern Mysore and Bangalore; Hyder sued for peace in 1772, paid 3.6 million rupees of arrears and 1.4 million a year, and ceded territory all the way to Bangalore; Tipu was sent to…

wars.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Hyder won at Pollilur (10 September 1780 on the Hyder Ali page, 27 August 1781 on the Kingdom page) and lost at Porto Novo; he died on 7 December 1782 and Tipu succeeded him.

wars.name: Maratha-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Ended in a peace agreement after Tipu's victory at Bahadur Benda; the terms are not on the page (the infobox says 1759-1787, the text 1785-1787).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: Began after Tipu attacked Travancore; the Treaty of Seringapatam of 18 March 1792 took about one-half of Mysore for the British, the Nizam and the Marathas and left two of Tipu's sons as hostages.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.outcome: The fort of Seringapatam was stormed on 4 May 1799 and Tipu killed; the Wadiyars were restored in a subsidiary alliance, ceding Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada to the British.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line; the Chikka Devaraja extent is a list of places (Medigeshi to Palni and Anaimalai) and the Hyder-era extent a river-and-ghats description ('bordered by the Krishna River in the north').

The 1792 treaty cedes named districts and territory up to the Tungabhadra River; the 1799 settlement names Coimbatore and Dakshina Kannada; the princely state's later boundaries are on no page opened and are taken as administrative lines.
